utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now if we can look at another document that was shown to you, P7058. I think this one can be displayed. It's not under seal. And if we look at paragraph number 3 together, and it's starts -- let me see, in the Serbian it starts [Interpretation] "The fact is that secret" -- [Microphone not activated] In the English, I will read what is said here by General Mladic: "It is true that secret military information is most frequently leaked through irresponsible and unprofessional use of existing communications which are generally not protected (such as PTT communications and a large proportion of military communications and communications of the RS/Republika Srpska MUP/Ministry of Interior, and also through undesignated use of portable radio sets without applying cryptographic data protection." Now, what the general is talking about here, is it implicating radio relay communications or other types of communications?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand what is written, sir, and I understand it to apply to all types of communications using electronic devices from wire communications, to radio relay. Regardless of the user, a civilian or a soldier, everyone is obligated to carry out measures of electronic protection.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And the specific items identified such as PTT and portable radio sets would those apply to radio relay transmissions?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: PTT communications also used multiple channel devices, but portable headsets were in private hands, and they were prohibited in the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we look at the next page in English and stay on this page in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Correction: Radio set, not headsets.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And we see it's the last line in the Serbian. And it says in order to present any further leakage of secret military information but using radio relay and PTT communications without applying measures of electronic and cryptographic data protection, I hereby order" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Slow down.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I apologise. "In order to prevent any further leakage of secret military information by using radio, radio relay, and PTT communications without applying measures of electronic and cryptographic data protection, I hereby order" -- And we have to go to the next page in Serbian. And then all these measures. Sir, looking at the measures that are ordered here, what effect would such measures have on the ability of someone else to continue listening in on transmissions at issue.

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, when you take these measures, the enemy or the person intercepting will certainly have less information and then they will also take measures to strengthen or intensify their surveillance to get more information.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Done with that document. Now if we can go into private session for the last several questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Colonel, I thank you for your patience and for trying to explain matters to us. I apologise for it taking longer than anticipated.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, have no further questions in re-direct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you Mr. Ivetic. Mr. McCloskey, any further questions for the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: In talking about simplex communications, we have seen some simplex communications for VRS radio communications. For example, RUP 12, the classic simplex -- or the RUP 12, for example, has a transmit button. In order to transmit, have you to press the transmit button and then you say something, hello, please come in, Crna Rijeka. You lift off and you can then receive a response and I think we've heard information that as long as you've got the transmit button down, you can't receive any response. Now, are you suggesting there's some kind of simplex conversation where two sides can talk over each other and overlap each other and not have to press a transmit button?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This specific device does not have such constraints, the one that was used by those who communicated in this recording.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And what specific device was used?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know of such a device.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, you said: "This specific device does not have such constraints, the one that was used by those who communicated in this recording." Now what specific device was used, was my question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand the question. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. How could you draw any conclusions as what was or was not possible with the device used?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, on the basis of the recording, I see that this is a device of some frequency below 100 megahertz with a lot of fading. That is to say, that the waves are bounced off, the participant who is closer to the station is heard well, the other one that is farther away fades away and that does not happen in radio relay communications, and that is not supposed to happen in radio relay communications.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Really, sir, tell us what radio, simplex radio we can buy that doesn't require us to press "transmit"?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I think that was asked and answered in the part - one moment. Actually answered page 63, lines 9 through 11.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It was, but it was such an outrageous claim it can be asked again, in my view.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You can put the question again, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Tell us, what simplex device is there in this world where you can talk without pressing "transmit" and then letting go?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not familiar with any type of radio device ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And you agree that this tape we heard, that was a radio transmission? Wasn't a phone-tap, a wire-tap.

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At any rate, no, because there wouldn't be any fading heard. And that is why I said it was radio and below 100 megahertz.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just to get matters now sharp, you say - than apparently is a conclusion - apparently the equipment allowed for speaking at the same time, but you are not aware of any such equipment existing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So, therefore, that it's possible just to interrupt each other on a simplex communication is something -- you have no idea whether there was any equipment that allows for that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes. Sir, on re-direct examination for the first time, you used this 65 ter 32891, page 21, that is the graph from Mr. Rodic's report and the if I am one that we could all read showed that the Vlasenica evaluation was at 620. And I'm -- I know at this point we all agree that getting the elevation of the reception point is important. So let me go to 65 ter 32924. Sir, recently in order -- we -- we sent an investigator to the Vlasenica headquarters with two elevation devices, and what you're about to see is a report on what those devices said at the location of the former Drina Corps headquarters. And according to those devices, it was at elevation above sea level of 672. And we can see that at -- I'm sorry, we don't -- didn't yet have an ability to translate it. But you can see the co-ordinates, north and east, and under that you see the term, 672. If we can go to the next page in the document. This is a picture of the building. Do you recognise that building? Have you been to that -- Drina Corps headquarters? This is a bit more recent. It may look a little more fixed up from the war days.

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I've already said that I just passed through Vlasenica and it was before the war at that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to the next page then. This is a different angle, a bit older, but I take it your answer is the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Do you recognise this building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. I've already said that I never walked through Vlasenica. I just passed through it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. If we could look at the next photograph. And that's just an aerial shot. Can you make any -- any sense out of that? Which is the actual co-ordinates from an aerial shot that gives us a feel for where it is in the town?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, in this image, I can see that the building is somewhere around the middle and by the river-bed or close to the river-bed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I would offer this into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honours, we would object. In so far as it's a statement of facts not in evidence I think the proper procedure would have to the Prosecution individuals examined or to have a site visit to the site because we got this for the first time last week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Given what was brought out and how it was -- particularly how it was brought out that I think having a record of the elevation and the location is important and having read it into the record is fine with me if counsel thinks this is a problem. If the Court wishes to accept this into evidence I think you have the power to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, the problem is --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... with authority.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'm not trying to say the Court doesn't have authority, I'm saying that the Court should consider that this is a Prosecution investigator going out there with a specific purpose. Now I would like to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... myself to measure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What is that purpose?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, the Prosecution's case is that the elevation is higher than the Defence says it is for the -- for that particular place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The document will be marked for identification. The parties are invited and urged to see whether they can agree on it. It's a matter of nowadays of GPS equipment. Choose the best you can. Put it at the bottom of that building and see whether it really 44.18 and 18.94 at an elevation of 672 and at the ground level. I mean, these are, I would say, you can argue all kind of other things, but this is a matter which seems to be similar like where London is located or New York or Paris or a certain building. So, therefore, the parties are really urged now to seek agreement on it and the Chamber would like to know if there's disagreement, would like to know what is wrong. And I just focus at this moment on nothing more than the location of the building which we see here and perhaps another question is, then, whether this is the building depicted in the previous paragraphs. If the parties could agree on that as well, that would also be appreciated.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I think the only issue is the elevation. That's the crux of what I was saying, is the elevation of the building [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... if that is the only thing there is no dispute about this being the position of the building as described by Mr. McCloskey. That's hereby then clear and put on the record. Then the only thing one has to do is send someone this with the three best GPS equipments you could think of and measure what the evaluation is and that's -- if it is a matter of 1 or 2 metres then we should not -- but if it is considerably different from what is here, then the Chamber would like to know. Meanwhile we mark the document for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can we go back to the first page. I know we went through it pretty quick.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: In that last paragraph, you can see that the investigator used two GPS devices and he describes them. So we got two. We didn't have three.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, perhaps the Defence has a better one. That's still possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'd like to hear within the next three weeks from the Defence as to whether there is a dispute about the elevation of this place. Marked for identification. Madam Registrar, under number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 32924 receives exhibit number P7508, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is marked for identification. Any further question, Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: How many?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I wanted to go over some of these -- well, this one more issue on the elevation which I think will be helpful, and some of the information that Your Honours were interested in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. We'll take a break and the next witness is then, I would say, excused and doesn't have to remain on stand by. Unless you would think could you finish it in ten minutes, ten to 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I doubt I can. I really will try. And if I get to the point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The next witness, Mr. McCloskey, even explaining why it takes more time, takes more time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The next witness doesn't have to remain stand by. We take a break, and we resume at quarter to 2.00. The witness may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey, you may continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Sir, can you agree with me that with a good former Yugoslavia topographic military map, one can reasonably determine elevation?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's look briefly at 65 ter 32894.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, we didn't get interpretation of the answer on the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You confirmed what Mr. McCloskey put to you, that you can reasonably determine and then I think it was elevation and not evaluation. I think I heard you confirm that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: You're not going to be able to -- it's too small a scale for us to sort out detail and I don't -- I don't want ask you to, but what I'm most interested in is can you tell from what you can see -- and let's blow up the bottom. I think it's the printing on the bottom that I think that is most important for these questions that we have the translation for to the right. So from what you see and we can -- well, we can read the translation -- oh. If we could blow that up that English part there. Thank you. It says: "Published and printed by the Military and Geographical Institute." And so is this the kind of military map that you have used and that the VRS has used in the past?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I used maps like these, but I mostly used maps with a scale of 1 to 100.000. This one is 1 to 25.000.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And we can see that. Thank you. That we see contour lines on this map. And according to the scale down here, that there is 10 metres between -- 10 metres of elevation between contour lines on this map; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Da. [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And now I'd offer this into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter 32894 receives exhibit number P7509, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now that map with the information on it was from the -- for the Zvornik area and so now I want to take us to a map that includes Vlasenica. It's also a 1 to 25.000 but it's a blow-up of the Vlasenica town area, and that is 65 ter 32922.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Maybe one more. That's good.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now, what we've done is we've gone to the map where they've written in on the -- the makers of the map have written on various contour lines the elevation, and we have these two ovals where we saw 600. So in those ovals, can you agree that those ovals reflect a 600-metre elevation for the area along those contour lines?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's drawn here. I see 600 -- oh, I apologise. First 600 metres, then 610, 620, 650, and the last is 680 at the centre near the church.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Right. But you'll agree with me that the written-in 600 in the oval is the elevation of that particular contour line noted as 600; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The arrow shows 680 metres at the contour line near the church.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yeah, I'm talking about the one in the black ovals we'll get to the church in a minute. The two black ovals, that says 600 in that oval, right, on that contour line? The black oval on left corner, that just means that contour is at 600 metres elevation.

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe I can't see well, sir, but it seems to me that it's written 800 and here below 810.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask whether the parties agree on that it's 600? Then you can put the follow-up questions to the -- Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I can't with this map, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You can't with this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I've got a map that you can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The whole of the city is indicated here as being at 680. Mr. Ivetic, would that change your mind as far as whether this could be 800?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, now Your Honours are asking about a different number, 680 I suppose the one in the lower left-hand corner means 801.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: No, below the word "Vlasenica."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Below the word "Vlasenica," yes, it says 680.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, it says 680, but what that is, I can't tell from this map, that's what I'm saying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... No, of course you can't. Of course not. It's usually an indication of the elevation, but of course, you can't tell for this map. Please proceed, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's consider for the purposes of these questions that this is 600 within this oval which I can tell you is clear on a map without all the electronics.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: If that is correct and it's 600 that would indicate that that contour line that it's written on is 600 metres elevation; correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You're referring to the top left corner, the oval here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I see that the witness is looking at the different position.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Look at the top left --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: If that says 600 on the contour line, according to the map makers that means 600 metres above sea level?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Da. [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I heard you say "da." I'm not sure that anyone else -- You agree that that 600 means in that oval is 600 elevation?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree, sir. And the terrain increases towards the centre. Along the contour lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, and I agree with you that it does increase. And if, as you've said previously and as we saw on that last map, if it increases in elevation for ten metres on each -- for each contour line by the time we get down near the -- the church, the church is at about 680 elevation; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And so we can also see that same contour line, it's a little -- it is hard to make out in this map. So the 672 estimate of the investigator is -- is consistent with this JNA map in terms of elevation, is it not?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey, I don't know how you're going to proceed, but to -- to draw conclusions as to the consistency of 672, this witness is not better qualified than the Chamber to do these kind of things. He has never seen this map before apparently. We can interpret the map not any less than the witness could.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I understood. It was just my way of getting so that you knew that that was my point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Yes. Okay. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. I would offer this map into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, I hear of no objections. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter 32922 receives exhibit number P7510.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is -- you're on your feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I would only ask that we get the original, the papers, so that we can actually make use of it instead of on the monitor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And I take it you have a paper copy somewhere, which allows Mr. Ivetic to check whether what is added to the map, those are the numbers whether that's accurately done, yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, and I think has had it in his computer but I know there's a lot in the computer so I can handle -- we can get this for him and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence and if any of the additions, Mr. Ivetic, meet some objections that is to the indication of the numbers related to the elevation lines, we'd like to hear from you within the next 48 hours. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now, if we go briefly back to your report, D1187, page 32. Should be 47 in the B/C/S. Okay. And I want to get into the third paragraph under the northern site. And what I want to ask you about is from the station at the northern site, there is optical and radio visibility towards the nodes at Veliki Zep, Cer and Crna Vrh. So I just want to confirm with you, from the northern site there is optical visibility to the Veliki Zep node?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And -- when you talk about the southern site in your report you don't note anything about the optical visibility between the southern site and Veliki Zep. But let me take you to Mr. Rodic's report, 65 ter 1D05805, page 19 in the English, page 16 in the B/C/S. And this is under seal as well. And looking at this 7.1.2, visibility profile, southern site, Veliki Zep, Mr. Rodic says: "There is an optical and radio visibility, and in that respect there are no obstacles for interceptions of communications from" -- Yeah, I'm at 7.1.2. Yeah, it should say there is no -- sorry. Let me just make sure we get this right. It says, "There is no optical and radio visibility and in that respect there are no obstacles for interceptions of communications ..."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: There is an optical.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: An optical, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: There is optical and radio visibility and there is no obstacle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that is consistent with there being no obstacles.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That's what I meant to say. Thank you for everyone helping on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So do you believe -- do you agree with Mr. Rodic there is no optic visibility problem, that there is optic visibility between the southern site and Veliki Zep?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And the Court has heard about the radio relay route, Veliki Zep-Vlasenica. So if there is optical -- if there is optical visibility to Veliki Zep, if there's a communication to Vlasenica from Veliki Zep, it can be picked up somewhere near Veliki Zep by both the southern and northern site, because Veliki Zep doesn't have any optical problems; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And so I think we can debate for a long time about how close it is to Vlasenica that we may or may not get into an optical visibility issue. But Veliki Zep was a good place to send your interception beams if you're the Muslim army; right?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I object to the representation that interception beams are sent somewhere. We have been talking for three days about how interception is done. There was no discussion of beams being sent somewhere and that's actually contrary to my understanding of the science involved.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you would rephrase your question but I take it that you wanted to know whether if you want to intercept whether Veliki Zep was a good place to do so for the Muslim army.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It's a good place -- I'll say point your beams.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: -- if that's better.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: It is not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Point your antennas.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's perhaps better. Would Veliki Zep be a good place to -- for interceptions to at least to focus on Veliki Zep to interceive communications?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, whoever is intercepting selected places from which they can receive, and towards whom a communication is sent doesn't matter, if I understood your question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. My question was that if you would focus on Veliki Zep, that that would be a good thing to do if you wanted to interceive.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And I would just -- and focus from the northern site and the southern site. That's the key part of this. Is that yes, you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I have nothing further, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: One small detail, if -- I did show a picture of the ribbon, and we have a picture of it just to get if we want to get that in the record so anyone reading it knows what I'm talking about. I leave that in your hands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You were showing the witness a ribbon. I think there's no dispute about it. That you did it ostensibly. And I don't think that anything put needs to be put on the record than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Mr. Dosenovic, this concludes your testimony because my colleagues have no further questions for you. I'd like to thank you very much for coming a long way to The Hague and for having answered all those many questions that were put to you, both by the parties and by the Bench, and I wish you a safe return home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... you may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have three minutes left. I'll briefly deal with a few matters which were still outstanding. I still have many, but let's try to get rid of a few. The first one is about Exhibit P3706. On the 11th of February of last year, 2014, Exhibit P3706 which is an excerpt from the minutes of the 63rd Session of the Kotor Varos Crisis Staff held on 7 July 1992 was admitted into evidence. On the 4th of May of this year, 2015, the Prosecution informed the Chamber by e-mail that the incorrect B/C/S original, bearing 65 ter number 02611, had been uploaded into e-court and uploaded a corrected version under 65 ter number 02611a. The Prosecution then requested the replacement of the original B/C/S version with the corrected version. This we have not heard of any objections by the Defence. The Chamber hereby instructs the Registry to replace the current B/C/S version of P3706 with the corrected version uploaded into e-court under 65 ter number 02611a. If there's any need to revisit the matter, you're invited to do so within the next 48 hour, Mr. Lukic. One very short, another one, about Exhibit P3468. The Chamber has identified a potential translation error in Exhibit P3468. The English translation of the document appears to be dated 2007 which does not correspond with the B/C/S version dated 1995. And the Chamber hereby invites the Prosecution to have the English translation verified and notify the Chamber and Defence accordingly. I leave it to that. We adjourn for the day, and we'll resume tomorrow, Wednesday, the 19th of August, 2015, 9.30 in the morning, in this same courtroom, I.
